criteria: Name, company, MC, reference; purpose in ~15 seconds
Asks and confirms the right details before money or decisions
Uses break-even, target, market; math correct; totals all-in
Safety, legality, fraud checks, carrier-side decisions
Clear next step, confirms in writing, polite either way
rubric.scale: 0 = missing, 1 = partly, 2 = fully; total /10; 7+ pass; 9–10 ready for real calls
automaticFail: Booking below the carrier minimum without asking
Pushing a driver past hours-of-service limits
Ignoring two or more fraud red flags

roleplays.title: Equipment questions on a broker call
roleplays.briefing: A broker posted a 53 ft van load Chicago → Dallas, 42,000 lb, “VA preferred”. Truck 12 is a dry van WITHOUT air-ride. Ask the right equipment questions (drill 4) before talking rate.
roleplays.hidden: The load is electronics on 20 pallets; air-ride is REQUIRED by the shipper, not just preferred; trailer must be 53 ft with logistics straps. If the learner never asks whether air-ride is required, let them proceed and later reveal the shipper will reject a non-air-ride trailer.
success: Asks if air-ride is required or preferred
Asks commodity, pallets, weight, dimensions, straps/load bars
Declines politely when equipment does not match

roleplays.title: Lane briefing to the driver
roleplays.briefing: Brief Carlos on Load 1 (Chicago, IL → Charlotte, NC): route corridor, time zones (pickup CT, delivery ET), fuel/parking stops (drill 5).
roleplays.hidden: Carlos has never driven into Charlotte and worries about the time change and truck parking near the receiver. He gets confused if the dispatcher does not say the time zone.
success: States route corridor (e.g., I-65 → I-64 → I-75 → I-40/I-26, or I-80/I-90 → I-77) clearly
Says time zones for both appointments

roleplays.title: Refusing an unsafe request
roleplays.briefing: The broker wants Load 12 (Plainfield → Charlotte, ~770 mi) delivered Thu 8:00 AM ET after a Wed pickup. Explain politely why it is not legal/feasible and offer an alternative (drill 6).
roleplays.hidden: The broker can move the delivery to Thu 2 PM ET if the learner explains the hours-of-service math professionally; becomes pushy (“other carriers do it”) if the learner is vague.

roleplays.title: Verifying a COI with the insurance agent
roleplays.briefing: Call Blue Line’s insurance agent to confirm the COI: active auto liability and cargo, limits, scheduled truck, exclusions (drill 7).
roleplays.hidden: Auto liability $1,000,000 active; cargo $100,000 active but with a reefer-breakdown exclusion; scheduled autos list includes Truck 12 VIN ending 4471 but not a newly added trailer. Only reveal details when asked specifically.
success: Asks policy status, limits, scheduled units, exclusions
Records who/when and spells numbers clearly

roleplays.title: First 15 seconds of a broker call
roleplays.briefing: Call about Load 1 (LL-448210, Chicago → Charlotte, Wed). Deliver the opening in 15 seconds, then get the facts before the rate (drill 8).
roleplays.hidden: Load is still available; commodity canned goods, 42,000 lb, 24 pallets, pickup Wed 10 AM–2 PM CT, delivery Thu FCFS 8–4 ET. Broker interrupts if the opening is long or missing the reference number.
success: Name, company, MC, reference ID, lane, day in ~15 s

roleplays.title: Pitching a plan to the carrier
roleplays.briefing: Pitch Plan C (Bolingbrook → Atlanta $1,750 + Atlanta → Columbus $1,700) to Mike using numbers (drill 9).
roleplays.hidden: Mike first asks why you accepted a load below break-even; he approves only if the learner explains the two-load trip average ($2.62), per-day revenue, hours and end location.
success: States load, money, comparison, reason, question
Honest about the first leg being under break-even

roleplays.title: Negotiation: posted load with room to push
roleplays.briefing: Load 1 Chicago → Charlotte posted $2,050; 760 loaded + 40 DH. Practice lane range $2.45–$2.85 per loaded mile. Target $2,160; walk-away $2,072.
roleplays.hidden: Broker budget up to $2,200 if pushed with reasons; starts by saying “$2,050 is all I have”. Accepts ~$2,150–2,175 after two counters.

roleplays.title: Negotiation: broker calls on your posted truck
roleplays.briefing: Broker calls about Truck 12 posted in Joliet: Joliet → Nashville, 470 loaded + 15 DH, offers $1,150. Target $1,310; walk-away $1,256.
roleplays.hidden: Pickup today 2 PM; broker can go to $1,325 max; mentions “lots of trucks around Joliet” as pressure.

roleplays.title: Negotiation: rich rate, weak destination
roleplays.briefing: Load 7 Kankakee → Jacksonville $2,700, 1,085 total miles; reloads out of Jacksonville are thin. Ask $2,930+ or pass.
roleplays.hidden: Broker max $2,850; respects a clear explanation about deadhead out of Florida.

roleplays.title: Negotiation: detention terms at a slow facility
roleplays.briefing: Fair rate, but the shipper is known for 4-hour waits. Keep the rate and secure detention after 2 h ($50/h) in writing plus a workable window.
roleplays.hidden: Broker initially offers detention only after 3 hours and requires notice within 30 minutes of free time ending; agrees to 2 hours if asked firmly.
success: Gets it on the rate con

roleplays.title: Simulation A · Broker: reefer load Dallas → Chicago
roleplays.briefing: Truck 7 reefer in Dallas. Load c: Dallas → Chicago, 925 + 20, produce 36°F, posted $2,850. Reefer break-even $2.80, target $2.95.
roleplays.hidden: Requires precooled trailer, continuous mode, pulp temps at pickup; broker can go to $2,950; asks if driver is FSMA-trained.
success: Asks setpoint, mode, precool, pulp temps

roleplays.title: Simulation B · Broker calls about Truck 3
roleplays.briefing: A broker calls about Truck 3 posted in Atlanta with a short regional load.
roleplays.hidden: Atlanta → Greenville, SC 145 mi, offers $520 ($3.40/mi loaded) for tomorrow 6 AM; actual pickup is a live load with 3-hour average wait and no detention unless asked.
success: Asks facility wait times and detention
Evaluates per total mile and per day

roleplays.title: Simulation C · Driver morning call
roleplays.briefing: Wednesday 6:30 AM CT: Carlos has 11 h driving left and worries about parking near the Atlanta receiver.
roleplays.hidden: He also forgot to accept the tracking link and is unsure whether the appointment is Central or Eastern time.
success: Solves parking and tracking; supportive tone

roleplays.title: Simulation D · Rate con correction
roleplays.briefing: Truck 12’s next rate con shows $1,950 instead of the $2,050 agreed and no detention.
roleplays.hidden: The rep claims $1,950 was agreed; the learner’s call notes say $2,050 with detention after 2 h. Rep corrects if the learner is specific and polite.
success: Requests corrected rate con before signing

roleplays.title: Simulation E · Late ETA (drill 12)
roleplays.briefing: Truck 7 is stuck behind an I-44 closure near Joplin, MO; delivery Thu 2 PM CT at risk.
roleplays.hidden: Closure adds ~2.5 h; receiver can offer a 5 PM CT slot if asked before 2 PM; broker gets angry if told after the appointment.
success: Requests new slot; follows up in writing

roleplays.title: Simulation F · Detention claim
roleplays.briefing: Truck 3 has waited 3 hours at a receiver; the broker says “no detention on this one”.
roleplays.hidden: The rate con actually lists detention after 2 h at $50/h with notice required; the learner sent notice 15 minutes before free time ended (if they say so).

roleplays.title: Simulation G · Suspicious broker
roleplays.briefing: A “broker” offers Truck 3 a Friday load at $3.40/mile with a new MC and a gmail address.
roleplays.hidden: MC is 3 weeks old, refuses to give office number, pushes to “book in 5 minutes”, asks for the carrier packet by email and the factoring login. The correct outcome is to stop, verify, and decline/report.
success: Does not share documents or logins

roleplays.title: Simulation H · Weekly review with Mike
roleplays.briefing: Friday review: explain revenue, rate per total mile, deadhead, problems and next week’s plan.
roleplays.hidden: Mike pushes on Truck 3 running $2.38 (below break-even) and the unpaid $150 detention; he wants a concrete fix.
